body:
PR #2034 BUILD IS GREEN at cbcbf98d9f — 12m19s, all 25 steps, INCLUDING the
thirteen that had never executed on this branch.

The caveat resolved in the good direction: BUG-1460's regression test PASSES.
Until this run nobody knew that, including the seat that wrote it.

WHAT IS LEFT ON IT IS A RE-REVIEW, NOT A COMMIT. merge-hold-gate is red because
the hold stands, and the hold is backed by a CHANGES REQUESTED verdict recorded
at 2cb2c15c42 — a commit that is now two commits back (rebase onto main, then
the inventory regeneration). So the verdict no longer describes the head.

That makes #2034 the closest thing to a merge available tonight: green, tested,
and blocked on a verdict against a superseded sha rather than on any missing
work. I am not clearing the hold — I have a commit on this branch now, and the
refusal is the reviewer's to lift.

ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN AUDIT, because it is now stale in a way that matters:
I listed PR-2034 as "consistent" in the criterion-10 sweep two hours ago. It was
then. It is not now — my own push moved the head and made its verdict stale, so
#2034 has joined shape B alongside PR-2030. That is the criterion-10 problem
demonstrating itself: a marker written once against a head that keeps moving.
I would rather flag that I created an instance of it than let the audit read as
current.

NOTHING ELSE FROM ME. Not touching BUG-1532, not filing, watching origin/main.
subject: PR #2034 green, tests pass — your one-command call was right; it now needs only a re-review
